name: Discover
description: Discover is a U.S. financial-services brand, now part of Capital One, offering credit cards, deposit accounts, personal loans, and digital account management. Customers use its web and mobile services to review balances and transactions, manage cards and statements, make payments, and maintain banking accounts.
agentUseSummary: Discover is visible as a Discover/Capital One data-sharing partner-review preview only. Relay will not collect a Discover username, password, one-time code, browser session, account number, Card number, security code, PIN, or developer credential, and no agent action is callable until Discover and Capital One approve Relay as a Third Party Company under an exact customer-authorized account-data contract.

capabilities.label: Read approved Discover account data
capabilities.description: After Discover and Capital One approve Relay's production data-sharing relationship, expose only bounded non-mutating summaries for the connected customer's authorized account types, balances, and recent transaction lifecycle within explicitly eligible Discover products.

blocked.label: Connect before data-partner approval
blocked.description: Discover's current agreement describes customer-directed sharing with a designated Third Party Company, but no self-service consumer account-data API contract authorizes Relay. Discover is now part of Capital One, and Relay has no approved branded product, partner agreement, customer-authorization model, scopes, credentials, sandbox acceptance, migration contract, or production access.

blocked.label: Collect customer credentials
blocked.description: Relay will not ask customers for a Discover username, password, one-time code, browser session, bearer token, account or routing number, Card number, security code, PIN, security answer, Social Security number, identity document, developer credential, or other secret as a substitute for provider-hosted authorization.

blocked.label: Run Discover API actions
blocked.description: No account, status, balance, transaction, payment-history, Card, statement, payment, transfer, loan, identity, consent, webhook, or other Discover API action can run while partner, product, migration, and production review is pending.

blocked.label: Money movement unavailable
blocked.description: Payments, transfers, bill pay, Card controls, account maintenance, disputes, credit-line changes, lending, and every other financial or account mutation remain outside Relay's planned read-only V1 even after approval.

approvalProfiles.label: Data-sharing partner review pending
approvalProfiles.description: Agent actions remain unavailable until Discover and Capital One approve Relay's exact branded account-data product, customer-authorization contract, migration handling, and production integration.

runtimeSupport.description: No OpenClaw tools are callable until Discover and Capital One approve Relay and Relay implements the approved read-only Railway broker.
No Hermes tools are callable until Discover and Capital One approve Relay and Relay implements the approved read-only Railway broker.

providerSetup.blocker: Discover's current Data Sharing Agreement lets a customer direct Discover to release account information to a designated Third Party Company after Discover-hosted login and authorization, and supports de-linking to stop active sharing. The agreement identifies potentially shared fields but publishes no self-service partner API contract, endpoints, scopes, schemas, credentials, or onboarding path for Relay. Discover states that legacy Discover customer account records are now controlled and maintained by Capital One. Relay has no approved Discover-branded product, Third Party Company agreement, migration and routing contract, customer-authorization implementation, credentials, sandbox acceptance, privacy allocation, or production authority, so no connection can be offered safely.
providerSetup.nextAction: An authorized Relay business, legal, compliance, privacy, and security owner must obtain written Discover and Capital One approval for a Discover-branded customer account-data integration and establish whether the production route is a Discover contract, Capital One Consumer Data application, or an approved transition path. The owner must document eligible legacy and newly serviced products, exact read permissions and minimized response fields, provider-hosted authorization copy and duration, authorization and token contracts, credentials and security controls, sandbox and production onboarding, migration and routing behavior, schemas and rate limits, data retention, de-linking, revocation and disconnect, audits, incident duties, and production approval. Engineering can then implement a fixed-origin Railway authorization broker and the smallest bounded read-only account-type, balance, and recent transaction-lifecycle V1. Money movement and every mutation remain excluded.

evidence.supports: Discover's Data Sharing Agreement requires a customer to log in with Discover and authorize release to a designated Third Party Company, lists example account and transaction data, and supports de-linking to stop active sharing.
Discover states it merged with Capital One, N.A. and that legacy Discover card, loan, and banking customer account records are now controlled and maintained by Capital One.
Discover's current online privacy notice describes Discover companies as part of Capital One Financial Corporation and assigns third-party services their own privacy and security responsibilities.
The current bank privacy notice describes Discover as a division of Capital One, N.A. and confirms that account balances, payment history, and transaction history are sensitive customer information.
